units.translation: They directed all the fire-hardened coins. Thus Hermannus for νό-μιμα τά [the customary things], which the scholiast explains as 'all the customs of the walled cities'.
law, custom; custom; musical mode
law, custom
custom
musical mode
But with new laws Zeus rules unlawfully.
ruling by his own laws
Such are the laws of the torch-bearers for me. Thus Schuetzius corrected what is read in M: τοιοίδ᾽ ἕτοιμοι [such ready ones].
For he has the punishment of a shamer, as is the law (thus Portus for νόμου [of law]).
contrary to the law of the gods
when their own citizens do not embitter the laws
you have ridden down the ancient laws

For this man is a suppliant of the house and a hearth-sharer of my house, where the first δόμων [of the house] (δήμων [of the people] in the first hand of M) was clearly introduced from the next line and Erfurdtius rightly changed it to νόμῳ [by law], as Sophocles OC 548 said νόμῳ δὲ κα-θαρὸς ἄϊδρις ἐς τόδ᾽ ἦλθον [by law I came here pure and unknowing].
I corrected to: especially since you, having prepared yourself by law, came as a suppliant pure and unharmed to my house, where ὅμως [nevertheless] was read for νόμῳ [by law].
by the law of the city
according to the laws of the house
who with hoary law makes straight the fate
just in marriages, where the scholiast says: 'according to the customs and opinions among you': hence Hermannus proposed ἔνδικοι νόμοις [just by laws].
as is the custom for mortals
With infinitive: 150: it is the custom for you to cull with lamentations.
it is the custom that the murderer be voiceless
but it is the custom that bloody drops demand other blood
by womanly custom
or did they come to the deed of children by custom?
with the customs of a Cissian wailing woman
This is another Hermes, according to the customs of the Greeks.
according to the laws of suppliants
let them make the bridegrooms gracious by their customs
the clear-voiced reed sounds a sleep-giving melody
the Curses raised the shrill cry
the muzzles whistle in a barbarian manner, where Prienus conjectured νόμον [melody].
you cry out around yourself a lawless melody
in shrill melodies

we shall establish a plucked wailing melody for the city. Thus Hermannus. γοήτων [of wailers] (γοητῶν [of wailers] by a later hand) νόμον [melody] (νόμων [of melodies] corrected) μεθήσομεν [we shall release] M. Suppl. 69 Ιαονίοισι νόμοισι [with Ionian melodies].
mind
and contracted νοῦς [mind] mind
always setting an unbending mind in anger
preserve your present mind
he grows old in mind, but his flesh is youthful
surely hearing that he will delight his mind
bronze is a mirror of the form, wine of the mind
mind
to be sick
to be sick
words are physicians for a sick anger, where since 'sick anger' is ineptly said, I wrote Ζεούσης [seething], about which see what is said under ζέω.

allow me to be sick with this sickness, where a corrector in one copy wrote τήνδε τὴν νόσον [this sickness], who did not know that older writers preferred the dative in this formula to the accusative: about which it is said in Thes. vol. 5 p. 1567.
for the sick it is sweet to know clearly the pain that remains
I would be sick, if it is a sickness to hate one's enemies
disease, evil
disease, evil
for somehow this disease is inherent in tyranny, not to trust friends
